title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted recordings without permission from the rights holders. The failure occurred during model development, before deployment of the public service. It would have been caught by securing licenses before training began, or by auditing training data sources against copyright registries.

The system generated music from text prompts after training on unauthorized material. Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group both sued and later settled with licensing agreements. Sony Music filed separate lawsuits alleging the system was trained on over 30,000 copyrighted songs. Independent artists also brought a class action lawsuit that a court declined to dismiss.

It is not established what specific mechanism Udio used to obtain training data, whether the company knew the material was copyrighted, or the outcomes of the pending litigation against Sony Music and independent artists.

summary:
# Summary

Universal Music Group has resolved its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio through licensing agreements. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs, including The Temptations' "My Girl," to train its artificial intelligence system without permission. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that uses only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, stream and share songs. The financial terms were not disclosed.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, allows users to generate original music from text prompts. This represents Udio's first licensing deal with a major record label. UMG's CEO stated the agreements show the company's commitment to artists and songwriters while embracing new technologies. Udio's CEO expressed enthusiasm about working with UMG to integrate AI and the music industry, noting that artists can opt into the new platform and will receive compensation, though specific details were not provided.
